A step function f is a function that can be written as a finite linear combination of indicator functions of intervals. In other words, f(x) = ∑_{i=1}^n c_i \mathbb{I}_{[a_i, b_i]}(x), where a_i, b_i are distinct points in [a, b] and c_i are constants.

To prove that f is Riemann Integrable, we need to show that the upper and lower Riemann sums converge to the same value as the partition of [a, b] is refined.

Let P be a partition of [a, b] into n subintervals [x_{i-1}, x_i]. Let f_i = f(x_i) be the value of f at the right endpoint of the i-th subinterval. Then, the upper Riemann sum is given by:

U(P, f) = ∑_{i=1}^n f_i (x_i - x_{i-1})

Similarly, the lower Riemann sum is given by:

L(P, f) = ∑_{i=1}^n f(x_{i-1}) (x_i - x_{i-1})

Since f is a step function, we have f(x_i) = f(x_{i-1}) for all i. Therefore, we can rewrite the upper and lower Riemann sums as:

U(P, f) = ∑_{i=1}^n f(x_{i-1}) (x_i - x_{i-1})
L(P, f) = ∑_{i=1}^n f(x_{i-1}) (x_i - x_{i-1})

Since the partition P is arbitrary, we can choose P such that the subintervals [x_{i-1}, x_i] are disjoint. Then, we have:

U(P, f) = ∑_{i=1}^n f(x_{i-1}) (x_i - x_{i-1}) = ∑_{i=1}^n f(x_{i-1}) (b_i - a_i)
L(P, f) = ∑_{i=1}^n f(x_{i-1}) (x_i - x_{i-1}) = ∑_{i=1}^n f(x_{i-1}) (a_i - a_{i-1})

Now, we can use the fact that f is a step function to show that the upper and lower Riemann sums converge to the same value. Specifically, we have:

U(P, f) = ∑_{i=1}^n f(x_{i-1}) (b_i - a_i) = ∑_{i=1}^n f(x_{i-1}) (b_i - a_i) = L(P, f)

Therefore, we have shown that the upper and lower Riemann sums converge to the same value, which implies that the step function f is Riemann Integrable.
